kf1.tip: Change the end of Stave 2 so Scrooge's cap fully puts out the Ghost's "bright clear jet of light". Write two lines on what that would say about his redemption.
kf1.note: A strong answer links the light to the truths that memory reveals. In the lesson the light still streams from beneath the cap. That shows Scrooge cannot fully suppress what he has seen, so change is still possible. If the light went out, it would suggest he could bury those truths, and his redemption would become far less certain. A weaker answer only says the scene gets darker and never says what that means for Scrooge changing.

kf2.tip: Argue for and against: "Scrooge pushes Fred away because he lost Fan, not because of greed." Give your strongest point each way, then decide.
kf2.note: For the statement, your strongest point is that Fred is the last living connection to Fan, the sister who loved Scrooge. Pushing Fred away may protect Scrooge from grief. Against it, Belle says a golden idol has displaced her, which shows greed drove him away from love. Most decide both matter. Loss explains why he rejects Fred in particular, and greed explains his wider isolation. A weaker answer argues one side and ignores the other.

cs1.tip: Find the weakest link in this chain: Ali Baba and Robinson Crusoe are tales of isolation and rescue, so young Scrooge had hope, so his weeping proves it survives. Say why.
cs1.note: Most would pick the first step. Reading Ali Baba and Robinson Crusoe shows escapism and imagination, but it does not prove Scrooge hoped for rescue himself. A lonely child might read simply to forget. The weeping step is also a jump, because tears could show regret rather than hope that has survived. A weaker answer attacks the facts, which are true, instead of the leap between them.
